title: Dynamic Route Price-Signal Proposal (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for adding a lightweight price-signal into the runtime routing decision. Goal is to let the ingress/router choose a model variant (or deployment tier) per-request using an explicit cost signal together with latency and quality estimates.

Context / motivation:
- We already route by latency SLO and tenant priority; customers have asked for predictable unit cost controls (avoid surprises on bursty usage).
- Price signals let us steer traffic toward cheaper variants when quality impact is low, and fall back to higher-cost models when quality matters.
- Important for Dedicated/reserved capacity and Hosted customers who want spending guardrails.

High-level idea:
- Attach a small numeric `price_budget` in request metadata (or derived from plan/rate-limits).
- Router computes an internal utility: u = alpha * quality_est - beta * latency_penalty - gamma * expected_price.
- Choose the route with highest utility while satisfying per-tenant budget constraints and global capacity rules.

Sketch: request metadata extension (proto-ish)

RequestRouteHint {
  tenant_id: string
  route_id: string // route-level config name
  price_budget_usd_per_1000: float // optional override from billing/plan layer
  priority_tier: int // 0..3 (0 = best-effort)
  latency_slo_ms: int // soft SLO
  quality_profile: "high" | "balanced" | "low" // hint for qualitative needs
}

Router response (informational)

RouteDecision {
  chosen_variant: string // e.g. redwood/llama-2-13b-8k-q4f16
  expected_price_per_1k: float
  expected_p95_latency_ms: int
  quality_score_est: float // 0..1 normalized score per route
  debug_tags: [string]
}

Decision algorithm (pseudo)

Inputs: request, candidate_variants[], tenant_budget_state, global_capacity_state
For each candidate v in candidate_variants:
  price = price_table[v].per_1k
  lat = latency_model.predict(v, request.seq_len_dist)
  quality = quality_lookup(v, request.quality_profile)
  utility[v] = wq*quality - wl*lat_penalty(lat, request.latency_slo) - wp*(price / request.price_budget_usd_per_1k)
Filter out variants that violate capacity or are disabled (rollouts/ab-tests)
Select argmax_v utility after applying hysteresis and safety net rules

Notes on components:
- price_table: periodically reconciled mapping from variant -> $/1k tokens (or normalized unit). Tied to Dedicated pricing or hosted list.
- latency_model: fast regression model (or lookup) using recent telemetry; must be robust to cold-start using model family defaults.
- quality_lookup: small mapping providing expected relative quality (0..1) for profile and task class. Can be bootstrapped from evals.
- lat_penalty: non-linear penalty for exceeding SLO; e.g., penalty = max(0, (p95 - slo)/slo)^2

Hysteresis / stability:
- avoid flipping variants per request: maintain per-tenant sticky window (30s) except when price budget exceeded by > 25% or latency SLO violated repeatedly.
- exponential backoff for optimistic cheaper variant re-tests.

Exploration / learning:
- sample 1-2% of traffic to cheaper variants even when utility slightly favors expensive ones (epsilon-greedy) to detect unseen regressions.
- log quality telemetry (human evals + automated evals) to refine quality_lookup.

Config sketch (Console):
- Route policy fields:
  * enable_price_signals: bool
  * default_price_budget_usd_per_1k: float
  * quality_priority_weight (wq): float
  * latency_weight (wl): float
  * price_weight (wp): float
  * sticky_window_s: int
  * exploration_pct: float

Operational considerations:
- Instrumentation: token_count, model_variant, chosen_route_tags, expected_price, actual_cost (post-billing), p50/p95 latency, quality_metrics.
- Alerting: sudden delta between expected_price and actual_cost; quality regressions after routing change; sustained SLO misses.
- Billing: router must not be authoritative for billing; price signals are advisory, final billing computed from actual model usage. But we surface estimates to the user and maintain reconciler to detect mismatches.

ASCII diagram (runtime)

Client/SDK --> Ingress --> Router[price-aware] --> ModelVariantPool --> Worker/GPU
                              | 
                              +--> TelemetrySink (sampling)
                              +--> CostEstimator service

Scenarios / examples:
1) Balanced app with default budget 0.06$/1k:
   - Candidate variants: v-cheap (0.03), v-medium (0.06), v-high (0.2)
   - Request: short chat, quality_profile=balanced, slo=200ms
   - Utility likely picks v-medium; occasionally routes to v-cheap for exploration.
2) Billing cap hit: tenant has monthly cap, budget for the day set low -> router favors cheaper variants aggressively, but with a safety cap that if latency SLO > 3x then fallback to higher-tier.

Edge cases / open questions:
- How to express price when variants use different token definitions (some bill by tokens, some by compute seconds)? Need normalization unit (e.g., normalized-cost-per-1k-tokens using model tokenization baseline).
- Who sets price_budget: client SDK vs billing service vs admin console? Propose hierarchical override: client_hint -> tenant_policy -> account_cap.
- Interaction with caching/prefixing: cheaper variant might be faster if KV cache hit - router should incorporate cache-hit probability into latency/price estimate.
- Privacy: we pass budget hints in requests; must ensure no leakage across tenants.

Rollout plan (minimal):
- v0: server-side-only boolean feature flag, price-aware router uses fixed price_table + basic utility with wq/wl/wp from config. No client-visible changes.
- v1: add route debug header that returns expected_price and chosen_variant for debugging.
- v2: UI controls in Console for per-route price_budget and weights.
- v3: integrate with billing reconciler and automated tuning of weights per route.

Evaluation / metrics for success:
- Unit cost delta (hosted): reduce median $/token by X% without increasing p95 latency by >Y% and quality regression <Z% measured by eval sets.
- Customer-facing: fewer billing surprises complaints; feature adoption of route-level budgets.

Small TODOs (me / follow-ups):
- [ ] Prototype utility function in routing service (get feature branch running)
- [ ] Create synthetic workload tests for price vs latency trade-offs
- [ ] Add price normalization doc (tokens vs time) and link to billing team
- [ ] Draft Console UX for route-level budget controls with product PM (Ravi)

References / links:
- INF-2147 (routing cost control RFC)
- existing route compiler notes (confluence) for where to hook weight params

Questions for reviewers:
- Is price signal best expressed as absolute budget or relative weight? (pros/cons)
- Should we include per-request max_cost_hard_limit that rejects if exceeded? Useful for very sensitive apps.
- How to avoid gaming from client hints? (server overrides required).

Bottom-line: price-aware routing is mostly an additive policy; start conservative, keep router advisory (not billing), instrument heavily, and iterate on normalization and safety nets.

Signature: Maya (working notes; not final)
